Tests ef-tags (entry filters)

Source: R/ef_tags.R
ef_test.Rd

This function is designed for testing ef-tags, i.e. entry filters that state under which condition an item is asked. An item with an ef-tag must be answered (not NA) in every row where its entry condition holds, and it must be NA in every row where the condition does not hold. The function checks both directions:

  • Test 1 (asked): test_var is not NA where condition is TRUE. Fails reveal underfiltering, i.e. the item was not asked although it should have been (or the interview was broken off before the item).

  • Test 2 (not asked): test_var is NA where condition is FALSE. Fails reveal overfiltering, i.e. the item was asked although it should not have been.

Values like -97 or -98 count as answered, only NA (and empty strings "" in character variables) count as not asked.

Usage

ef_test(
  data,
  test_var,
  condition,
  check = c("both", "asked", "not_asked"),
  use_duration = TRUE,
  print_filter_vars = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A neps field-data dataframe.

test_var

A string with the name of the item that carries the ef-tag. Can also be a character vector of several items that share the same entry condition.

condition

The entry condition as an unquoted R expression, e.g. h_panel == 1 & !alintrop %in% 2. Use TRUE for items that are always asked. Objects from your script (e.g. a vector of codes) can be used too. A single string with the expression is accepted as well, e.g. "h_panel == 1", and so is a variable that holds a string or a quoted expression, e.g. cond <- quote(h_panel == 1), which is handy if several items share a condition.

check

Which direction to test: "both" (default), "asked" (only Test 1) or "not_asked" (only Test 2). "not_asked" can be useful if many interviews were broken off and Test 1 is therefore not informative.

use_duration

Logical, if TRUE (default) Test 2 tolerates a value when the corresponding duration variable is 0 or NA. If FALSE, Test 2 fails for every value where the condition is not met. Has no effect for items without a duration variable.

print_filter_vars

Optional character vector. Additional variable names to be included and prioritized in the printed output when errors are detected. Variables used in condition are always printed next to test_var.

Value

Invisibly returns TRUE if all tests pass, otherwise stops with an error after printing the problematic cases.

Details

condition is an R expression that is evaluated inside data, so it can combine several variables freely. To translate the PV syntax, use:

  • x = 1, 2 becomes x %in% c(1, 2)

  • x <> 2 becomes !x %in% 2 (this is also TRUE if x is missing, like in the CATI logic)

  • x <> . becomes !is.na(x) and x = . becomes is.na(x)

  • & and OR become & and |. Several if lines of one ef-tag are alternatives and are combined with |.

Prefer %in% over == and !=: comparisons with ==, !=, < or > return NA if a variable is missing. Rows where the condition is NA are treated as "condition not met", and the function prints a note how many rows that affected.

The ef-tag of an enclosing block (e.g. "Beginn Block 2") applies to all items in the block. Either add it to condition with &, or filter data to the block condition beforehand, as you would with the other test functions.

With use_duration = TRUE (default), a value in Test 2 is tolerated if a corresponding duration variable (<var>duration, scr_<var>duration or src_<var>duration) exists and is 0 or NA, because this means the item was not shown, like in af_test_complex(). This matters for items that are filled by an autoif without being asked, e.g. an end date that is set to the interview date if the episode is ongoing. Month and year variables of a date (e.g. alendm, alendj) have no duration variable of their own, so the duration variable of the date is used instead (e.g. scr_alenddatduration). The output names the duration variable that was used. Set use_duration = FALSE for a strict Test 2 that ignores duration variables.

See also

Other test functions: ac_test(), date_test_complex(), label_test(), value_label_test()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# aliz: --ef: if (h_panel = 1)
ef_test(T_27AL, "aliz", h_panel == 1)

# aliz2: --ef: if (h_panel = 0 & h_dauertan = 2)
ef_test(T_27AL, "aliz2", h_panel == 0 & h_dauertan == 2)

# almb: --ef: if (almod1 = 1, 2, 4), within Block 2 with --ef: if (alintrop <> 2)
ef_test(T_27AL, "almb", !alintrop %in% 2 & almod1 %in% c(1, 2, 4))

# alenddat: two ef lines are alternatives: if (h_panel = 0) / if (aliz = 2)
ef_test(T_27AL, c("alendm", "alendj"), !alintrop %in% 2 & (h_panel %in% 0 | aliz %in% 2))

# only check for overfiltering
ef_test(T_27AL, "alge", alme %in% 1, check = "not_asked")

# item that is always asked (--ef: alle)
ef_test(T_27AL, "alnr", TRUE)

# codes defined in the script can be used in the condition
panel_modes <- c(2, 3)
ef_test(T_27AL, "alintro12", almod1 %in% panel_modes)

# strict Test 2 without the duration rule
ef_test(T_27AL, "algb", almb %in% 1, use_duration = FALSE)
} # }
